- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ levels), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, particularly after mid-forecast period.
- Model underestimates true price drops during sharp declines (e.g., 80→60 range), often by 5–10 points.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical mean reversion — tends to hold forecasts too high during “high” periods and too low during “low” periods.
- Model shows lagged response to recent price movements — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a spike.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts often spike upward after minor price corrections, then fail to correct.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price corrections after major spikes — especially in the 30-day horizon, where true drops are steeper than forecasted.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp reversals and overestimates gradual declines.
- Model exhibits “anchor bias” — often starts from recent high prices and fails to adjust downward even when true price is falling.
